samples.identification: Unpacked x86 Windows HTTP command-shell implant, with rebuilt imports and retained UPX section names; no family attribution established.
evidence: Entry 0x2a70ef reaches main 0x2a5ce0 and initialization 0x2a3fb0; XOR-0x0f decoding resolves APIs and both configured HTTP endpoints. main repeatedly calls HTTP worker 0x2a5850. Endpoint hostnames are not required by the detections.

The command worker at 0x2a51xx creates a pipe at 0x2a5238, assigns its write handle to STARTUPINFO stdout/stderr and uses flags 0x101. At 0x2a52a5 it formats system-directory/cmd.exe /c with the supplied command and calls CreateProcessA at 0x2a52d9. It reads the pipe at 0x2a5326, transforms the output, and sends it through 0x2a42e0 at 0x2a5369.

Installation 0x2a3cc0 reads its own image, creates AhnLab-named directories, writes the executable under ProgramData (or Common Files fallback), writes a CurrentVersion/Run value through dynamically resolved registry APIs, and launches the copied image. The chosen product names corroborate the disguise but do not gate the rule.

After installation, 0x2a6097 reads the current module path, builds /c del /q with that path, resolves ComSpec and ShellExecuteA, then launches the hidden deletion command at 0x2a6112. This supports the new cleanup objective.

Remote allocation/write/thread APIs are XOR-hidden in the same command implant. The retained injection finding accurately describes this API set; it does not assert successful runtime injection. The SEH E9 patch sequence in the supplied code supports the retained self-modification finding.
samples.context_missing: No deployment authorization, live network success or external family corroboration; the concealed command interface and disguised persistent installation tip the verdict.

samples.identification: Obfuscated AutoIt RunPE loader carrying a native security-sabotage loader and an embedded UPX-packed XMRig-derived miner.
evidence: Lines 6 onward concatenate a 3009536-byte PE as hex in $X. Function aliases at lines 3056-3076 resolve the indirect calls; line 3077 invokes EBNDPEJIPFUNC($X). Random declarations and AutoIt startup callbacks are padding around the active loader.

The active function defaults to Windows/explorer.exe, calls CreateProcessW with CREATE_SUSPENDED=4, gets thread context, parses PE headers and sections, allocates remote RWX memory, conditionally unmaps the original image, fixes relocations and copies the replacement image. It rewrites PEB.ImageBaseAddress and Eax/Rcx to the replacement entry, then sets context and resumes.

WriteProcessMemory is assembled from an 18-character array at line 3339. On x64 Windows 24H2, lines 3291-3327 resolve ZwManageHotPatch and an RtlEqualUnicodeString-relative address and write 48 31 C0 C3 (xor rax,rax; ret) into the child before ResumeThread. These are active patch paths, not interpreter API vocabulary.

The embedded PE entry reaches 0x140028ba0. Independent initialization-block emulation recovers additive-obfuscated strings. Native registry/child-process paths target Defender Security Center notifications, Defender exclusions, SystemRestore DisableSR/DisableConfig, reagentc /disable, sc stop UsoSvc/bits/dosvc, and update-service backup/rename keys. This is security/recovery sabotage, not ordinary miner operation.

At 0x14002c8ec the native loader passes a 0x29b000-byte embedded buffer to 0x140028640. That function XOR-decodes using a reconstructed 32-byte repeating key, Base64-decodes, and XOR-decodes again (second XOR call at 0x140028897), recovering a 2049024-byte UPX PE. It maps that image into another Explorer process and adjusts context and protections.

UPX decompression recovers a 5664768-byte native miner with XMRig RTTI, RandomX code, mining/Stratum command configuration and pool handling. Miner identity alone is dual use; the parent loader security sabotage and covert image replacement establish hostility. Resource version 4.7.0 is a claim, not independently verified upstream provenance.
samples.context_missing: No consent/deployment context or observed runtime success. The nested loader security sabotage and concealed process replacement outweigh legitimate miner and RunPE-library explanations.
changes: Add typed AutoIt suspended creation, remote RWX allocation, cross-process read/write and unmap capabilities.

Correct five findings that matched arbitrary hex-decoded native bytes: wordlist x2, wildcard key, local shell redirection and scored filename IOC table. Syntax/list rules now read original source bytes; preserve true source controls.

coverage_gap.limitation: The source is unparsed text with fragmented hex. Current facts do not reconstruct the complete PE and its arithmetic-obfuscated UTF-16 constants as recursively analyzed layers. The nested XOR/Base64/XOR stage also requires code-dependent key recovery. Matching one selected ciphertext key, collector name or exact payload size would be specimen-specific. Preserve this as a decoder/coverage gap rather than claiming runtime success or adding duplicate hostile composites.

samples.identification: review-library 1.0.0, a renamed 581-byte archive of incomplete Rust token/App-Bound-key API examples.
evidence: Archive contains only Cargo.toml, src/token.rs and src/crypto.rs. Cargo manifest has build=false, no dependencies and no target; there is no src/lib.rs or src/main.rs. The examples contain unresolved imports, variables and LocalState fields and are not a runnable crate.

worker() lists lsass.exe and winlogon.exe and contains OpenProcessToken, DuplicateToken, ImpersonateLoggedOnUser and RtlAdjustPrivilege calls using unresolved parameters; there is no process selection feeding those calls or invocation of worker(). The existing suspicious trait says cloning beside process-name references and is accurate.

crypto.rs has APPB/v20 constants and app_bound_encrypted_key plus CryptUnprotectData, NCryptOpenKey and NCryptDecrypt calls with unresolved inputs. No browser store is opened, no key is read, and no decrypted data is sent anywhere. The archive-level suspicious co-occurrence finding accurately states that it pairs these primitives with token impersonation; it does not claim theft.
Every remaining notable finding corresponds to the API call, key field, byte prefix or process-name reference actually in the source. Retain all of them.
samples.context_missing: No authentic upstream identity, deployment context or larger surrounding program. These fragments demonstrate dangerous dual-use mechanisms but contain no concrete hostile action; the supplied bytes favor benign examples.
changes: No Rust traits changed; preserve 2 suspicious root findings, 1 suspicious token.rs finding and all notable capabilities.
